Hi Marta / Diego,

Thanks — great to see the PO format. Short answers up front, then specifics below:

- PO fields: we require PO number, billing entity name, remit address (or wire remit instructions), and tax ID/BU code. We can map PO line numbers to our invoice line items (we do this for enterprise customers).
- Invoice cadence: monthly consolidated invoices are our default for enterprise; we can support weekly or bi-weekly split invoices but there is an operational delta (extra invoices = additional processing).
- Net terms: Redwood standard is Net30. We can extend to Net45 or Net60 for customers with a committed annual spend or a purchase order with preauthorization. For Net60 without commitment, we usually request a small uplift or a short prepay buffer.

Options for Helios to consider:
1) Monthly consolidated billing + PO line mapping (no change to list price)
2) Monthly consolidated billing + 12-month commitment = Net45 + 2% volume discount
3) Weekly split invoices (per PO line mapping) = Net30, or Net60 with a ~1.5% SOF (short-term financing) fee to cover ops.

I attached our onboarding checklist (Redwood_PO_Onboarding_Checklist.pdf) — it lists the exact JSON fields we can accept in the EDI/XML export and the CSV template for PO line mapping. If you can confirm which option Helios prefers, we’ll draft the pricing amendment and a sample invoice export for your AP to validate.

Karthik Iyer
